title: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

sense.text: Today’s class is Revelation 21, Thy Kingdom Come, and it opens with the Lord’s Prayer. “Hallowed be thy name”: that’s Hebrew; sometimes it comes out like it’s English, but it’s not. It means honoured be thy name.

“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven”: the thought of understanding is that the kingdom is coming on earth. Many Christians say when I go up to heaven; that is not what the Lord said. You’re not going to the upper room. The scripture says in earth. Reading is fundamental.

precepts.why: “As the days of heaven upon the earth”: that’s what I want. Can we write these preachers a letter and let the congregants know: you are not growing wings, flying up to the by and by, playing harps on clouds, eating catfish and smoking cigars. That’s not happening. Everything will be on earth.

sense.text: “And I saw a new heaven and a new earth”: the next Christian thought is that the earth and the heavens will explode and be gone. All it means is a change of worlds, a change of kingdoms. “For the first heaven and the first earth were passed away”: the kingdoms we know today, the United States of America, France, Germany, the UK, are all going to be cast down. “And there was no more sea”: there ain’t going to be no water on the planet? No. The sea is the multitude of nations rebelling against the Most High, and they are all going to be subdued under this new kingdom that’s coming.

precepts.why: Regarding the new earth. “One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh”: meaning those souls always come back; that’s for another class, but it’s telling you about regeneration. “But the earth abideth for ever”: the earth does not go away and come back like generations do.

A change of worlds. “I beheld till the thrones were cast down”: the kingdoms on the earth cast down, destroyed. “The Ancient of days did sit”: the Most High, having no end of days nor beginning of days. “Whose garment was white as snow”: in order to have a garment you need a body to put a garment on, so God does have a body. “The hair of his head like the pure wool”: he got hair on his head, and it’s not long, stringy hair; it’s like the pure wool.

A precept for “there was no more sea”. “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas”: it compares the multitude of many people to the noise of the seas. “The rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters”: it’s nations going and rebelling against the Most High God. That’s why there’s no more sea in this new kingdom: they’re all going to be subdued.

sense.text: “The holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven”: like it said, thy kingdom come, people think it’s going to come out the sky. That’s not what it’s talking about. “Prepared as a bride adorned for her husband”: here’s the key. Jerusalem is a people before it’s a place. The Lord is not marrying a place; he’s marrying a people. So this great city coming from heaven is symbolic of the people first and foremost. For those of you that think the kingdom’s going to come from the sky, you think you’ll be walking down the street one day and see it coming: that’s not happening. This is why the Lord said you must read his word precept upon precept.

precepts.why: “The secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is”: the secrets of wisdom is what we want. Many times we read scriptures and there are dual meanings behind it, and this verse is one.

The duality of New Jerusalem. “And pray unto the Highest continually, then will I come and talk with thee”: this is the archangel Uriel speaking to Esdras. Esdras was fasting, eating the herbs of the field, and the Lord was about to show him many things.

Esdras was talking to a woman crying for her dead son. “Her face upon a sudden shined exceedingly”: all of a sudden she begins to glow. “Suddenly she made a great cry very fearful: so that the earth shook at the noise of the woman”: you got to imagine this thing; the earth is shaking, like what the hell is going on here. “The woman appeared unto me no more, but there was a city builded”: the woman he was talking to transformed into a city, and Esdras is like what the hell am I seeing. Then he cries out, “Where is Uriel the angel”.

Uriel explains what happened with the woman. “This woman, whom thou sawest is Sion”: this woman is really a city, and vice versa. So when we read Revelation 21 about this great city coming from heaven, it is symbolic of the people first and foremost.

“Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion”: he’s telling us to wake up and put on our strength. “Put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city”: how is a city going to put on garments? This city represents the people. “There shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean”: meaning the other nations.

Another precept for the bride. “Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am married unto you”: married unto who? The Israelites. “I will take you one of a city, and two of a family”: meaning the elect; everybody ain’t coming on this trip. “And I will bring you to Zion”: so he’s married to the people.

Christ said the kingdom does not come with observation. “The kingdom of God cometh not with observation”: you’re not going to see it; it’s not coming from the sky. “Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there!”: it’s coming from the east, no, it’s coming from the west; Christ said that ain’t what it’s talking about. “The kingdom of God is within you”: you Israelites, you’re the kingdom of God, you’re the holy city, you’re New Jerusalem. That was a hard thing for our people to grasp, and it’s still hard.

sense.text: “Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people”: that’s some heavy stuff. This is the same exact thing Moses said, so for you to think the Old Testament and New Testament are saying two completely different things, you’re insane. You’ve been Christianised, bamboozled, hoodwinked, bird boxed. The men he’s talking about are you, the Israelites.

precepts.why: Moses said the same thing. “If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments”: when we were entering the promised land, if we keep God’s commandments the land will be full with blessings, and we will eat to the full. “I will rid evil beasts out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land”: no evil beast and no war in your land. “Five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight”: you need power to do that thing; some of you can’t get the old raggedy woman off the block. “For I will have respect unto you”: he has respect for those that keep his law. “Ye shall eat old store”: the crops would last us from the old season to the new. “And I will set my tabernacle among you: and my soul shall not abhor you”: that’s what we were just reading in Revelation; he will not hate us. “I will walk among you, and will be your God, and ye shall be my people.”

A side note on Leviticus 26:9, because Christians love to go to Acts 10. “God is no respecter of persons”: they say the Bible contradicts; no, the white man contradicts the Bible, and because you believe everything he says you’re confused. That respect is for those Israelites that keep his law. “But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness”: who was in every nation? The next verse tells you: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel”. The children of Israel were scattered in all nations, from the time of slavery and from the time of the Assyrian and Babylonian captivity.

sense.text: “And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes”: for you not to want the kingdom, you’re insane, with all the pain and sorrow we go through day by day, year by year, decade by decade. “Neither shall there be any more pain”: that foot that hurt you, that back, that rheumatism and arthritis are going to be gone in that day. Y’all can get rid of them canes. “For the former things are passed away”: this goes back to verse 1, the new heaven and new earth, for the old was passed away. The former things involved the pain and the sickness.

precepts.why: What Isaiah prophesied. “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth”: that’s what we just read in Revelation 21:1. “I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy”: the Lord is going to change everything. “The voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her”: ain’t going to be no more stillbirths, no more miscarriages. “The child shall die an hundred years old; but the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed”: this goes with the other nations and those of our people that’s not part of that first resurrection. “They shall not build, and another inhabit”: those days of captivity ain’t happening no more. “Before they call, I will answer”: you think he don’t listen; on this day he said before they call I will answer. “The wolf and the lamb shall feed together”: that’s how you know this is the kingdom. Moses said the Lord will remove all evil beasts out of the land, so he is going to change the whole nature. “They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain”: the other nations are going to be at their very lowest state.

sense.text: “Behold, I make all things new”. “Write: for these words are true and faithful”: write, for the things I’m saying are true and faithful, meaning they will surely come to pass.

“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end”: many people ask why Christ says I am Alpha and Omega. That’s Greek for the beginning and the end. If you catch it you catch it; if you don’t, you don’t. “I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely”: you got these movies looking for the Fountain of Youth, but this fountain ain’t what they think it is. The water represents the word of God.

precepts.why: Why Christ is the beginning and the end. “The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit”. “Howbeit that was not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural”: the first Adam wasn’t spiritual; then came the spiritual Adam. “The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.” If you catch it you catch it; get a clue, stay in the spirit.

“Being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli”: Joseph was not the son of Heli; Joseph was the son-in-law to Heli. Matthew 1 gives you Joseph’s genealogy to Christ; Luke 3 gives you Mary’s genealogy through her daddy Heli.
“Which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God”: boom. You catch it you catch it; you don’t, you don’t.

For the Corinthians precept, where it said the first Adam was natural. Why did Adam fall? Why did he listen to Eve? “For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” That opens up another door, which I’ll touch on in another class.
The fountain of the water of life. “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”: so the water represents the word of God.

sense.text: “He that overcometh shall inherit all things”: you have some Israelites that say they already overcame. Then why are you on welfare? Why are you in the ghetto? If you overcame, why is the white man telling you to shut up and sit down? “And I will be his God, and he shall be my son.”

precepts.why: “For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world”: to be born of God means to be born again, meaning changed, converted. John makes it more plain here; he says the world, whereas in Revelation he goes into more metaphoric speech, like the mark of the beast, the image of the beast and the number of his name. “This is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.” “He that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God”: if you believe that Christ is the Son of God, don’t worry, you have overcome the world.

Everybody says they believe: I believe, I believe, I believe I can fly. “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment”. When you see men and women run up out of here saying to hell with Matthew 18, I’m not doing it, they don’t believe Jesus is the Son of God. They can say they believe all day on Facebook; your actions have spoken for you. Soon as the conflict came, you ran, high-tailed it out of here.

Examples of he that overcometh, because John was very generic. The churches are the Israelites scattered throughout Asia Minor. “He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death”: we touched on that last week. If you have part in the first resurrection, the second death has no power over you.

“To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna”: that’s that secret understanding. “And will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it”: he’s going to give those of us that make it a new name, and when you hear it your spirit is going to say that’s you, your name from the beginning. No, your name ain’t Yolanda, it ain’t Raheem, it ain’t Julio.

“He that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end”: unto when? Till death do we part, either your death or Christ’s return, whichever comes first. It’s not until you get sick and tired of it; this is a lifelong journey. Some say I’ve been doing this seven years: don’t compare your chapter seven to our chapter 30. “To him will I give power over the nations”. “He shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”: we are going to break the nations and make them submit. “Even as I received of my Father”: Christ said, I received it of my Father, and I’m going to give it to you.

To explain his works. “But his law have they despised, and denied his covenants; in his statutes have they not been faithful, and have not performed his works”: so his works refers to his law, his statutes, his covenant.

About Christ. “Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.” “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance”: Satan in Matthew 4 showed him all the kingdoms of the world and said I’ll give you all this if you bow down and worship me, and Christ said get behind me. Now watch what the Father says to Christ: I’ll give you the nations. “Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel”: that’s the same thing Christ says to us in Revelation 2.
That’s why another scripture says we are joint-heirs with Christ. “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”.

You might think joint-heirs leaves out the woman, but it doesn’t. “Dwell with them according to knowledge”: according to the knowledge of God, the law. “Giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”: yeah, we know she got half a clue, but bear with her. “And as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered”.

Still dealing with he that overcometh. “Clothed in white raiment”. “I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels”: that’s the honour, for Christ to confess your name before the Father and the angels.

“Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God”: to be a pillar means to be a leader. “He shall go no more out”: out into captivity; that ain’t happening no more. “The name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven”: that’s how beautiful it’s going to look. “And I will write upon him my new name”: Christ said I got a new name too, and I’m going to give it to you. So what are y’all fighting for, Yahawashi, Yahushua, Emmanuel? You say that, you’re damned? He just said I got a new name that I’m going to give you.

“To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne”: that’s heaven. No, you ain’t going to be sitting on equal level with Christ; it’s going to be order. The law is about order. We all equal is Negro thinking, and only when we get around each other; when you get around white folks you know your place.

sense.text: Going through the verse word by word. “But the fearful”: woe to the double-minded. “And unbelieving”: those who question with doubt; how was Jonah swallowed by the whale, that don’t make no scientific sense. Then go to hell; jump into the lake of fire. “And the abominable”: the abominable customs of Leviticus 18. “And murderers”: whosoever hateth his brother. “And whoremongers”: a sexually promiscuous man. “And sorcerers”: a coconut under the bed, a pile of salt in the corner with a glass of wine, the newspaper opened to the horoscope, chicken bones around the neck; you see that in Haiti, Jamaica, Trinidad and the Dominican Republic. If your mother is buying a bottle of water for healing from the pastor, or getting the prayer cloth to heal her cancer, that’s sorcery. “And idolaters”: covetousness, the love of money. “And all liars”: them that did the edited videos. “Shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death”: in essence, you’re going to die. We’re not wishing death on nobody; we’re telling you what the scripture says.

precepts.why: The fearful. “Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goeth two ways!”: you’re double-minded. You got the Bible in your hand, but you won’t do nothing it says.

The unbelieving. We just read in Ecclesiasticus 32 that if you believe, you keep the commandments. “Unto the pure all things are pure”: whatever the Bible says, they believe it, accept it and do it. “But unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled”: that’s why we ain’t got time for people always questioning. The questions ain’t regular questions; they’re questions of doubt, questions of non-belief.

“Him that is weak in the faith receive ye”: some brothers have weaker faith than others, so you deal with them at first. “But not to doubtful disputations”: there’s a limit to that. Disputation means they want to argue with you; show them the door.

The abominable. “That ye commit not any one of these abominable customs”: don’t keep any one of these abominable customs. Let’s read some of them that some of us, here and online, might be involved with.

“The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother”: to have sex with your mom is abominable; the father’s wife is your stepmother; then your sister. “Thy son’s daughter, or of thy daughter’s daughter”: your grandchild. Everybody’s family got that nasty granddaddy you don’t want your kids staying with. Then your stepsister, your aunts, your daughter-in-law, your sister-in-law. “A woman and her daughter”: some of you are dealing with the mama and the daughter both; the Bible says that is abominable. “Neither shalt thou take a wife to her sister”: having two women, a ménage, a threesome; you can’t do that. “As long as she is put apart for her uncleanness”: you’re supposed to wait seven days; don’t run the red light, and you women be giving into that thing. “Lie carnally with thy neighbour’s wife”: that’s adultery. “Pass through the fire to Molech”: what were they doing with their children? Killing them. The new word today is abortion; do not abort your babies, that is abominable. “Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind”: marriage helps, but if you know you are still battling with that same sex demon, don’t get married yet; get counselling, pray and fast, and get that demon out. “Neither shalt thou lie with any beast”: that’s bestiality, and it’s nasty; that’s abominable. Then, verse 30: keep mine ordinance.

Murderers. We love to say we don’t murder; the group that ran up out of here said they don’t murder. “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer”: if I record any of you and hold it for two to three years and wait to embarrass you on YouTube, that is hatred. You say you don’t hate anybody; that’s a lie. You will have your part as a murderer in the lake of fire.

Whoremongers. A whoremonger is a person who has dealings with prostitutes, and especially a sexually promiscuous man, what was called in the class a cockman: babies everywhere, women everywhere, and he don’t take care of one. All you good-looking brothers fall under this. “All bread is sweet to a whoremonger”: he don’t care what she looks like; whatever comes by, he will sleep with it. It’s about him and his sexual fulfilment for the moment.

A whoremonger is expert at finding a stupid woman. “Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away.” “Which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts”: stupid women filled with sin.

Many of you will say I don’t practise sorcery or idolatry. Everybody got quiet with that one because you know your mama’s in the sorcery. “For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft”: you don’t want to apply Matthew 18 with your brother and your sister; you are rebellious. “And stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry”: you’re stubborn to do what God says; that’s idolatry, as if you worship Buddha or Shango.

Idolatry. “Mortify therefore your members”: mortify means to deaden. “Fornication”: sexual immorality, the Leviticus 18 we just read. “Uncleanness”: that’s Leviticus 15. “Inordinate affection, evil concupiscence”: messing with your brother’s daughter. “And covetousness, which is idolatry”: this is the part I wanted. If you have a covetous spirit, you are an idolater.

What covetousness means. “For the love of money is the root of all evil”: it don’t say money; it says the love of it. My business, my money, they destroyed my business: the whole scheme in them videos was money. “Which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith”: we are witnesses of what has occurred with former brothers and former sisters who have erred from the faith. A brother in the class gives an example: the objective of Matthew 18 is to win your brother back, but they came with suspicion to set him up for their own lust. “And pierced themselves through with many sorrows”: it’s not us piercing them; they pierced themselves. If your business can only thrive in IUIC, it’s a hustle, not a business. Business dealings in Israel are conditional upon keeping the laws of the Most High; once you break them, you destroyed your relationship with the nation of Israel, and the business is over.

All liars. If you record somebody and the cup jumps from point A to point B on the video, that’s editing; they chopped the video up to make you sound like you’re saying something. “Devise not a lie against thy brother”: devise means to plan or invent a complex procedure, system or mechanism by careful thought: video editing. Its synonym is fabricate, to invent or concoct something typically with deceitful intent. “Neither do the like to thy friend”: these are people we knew for years. “Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good”: a custom is a habit; it wasn’t one time, it was multiple times.

sense.text: Another speaker in the class: the scripture says the wages of sin is death. Everybody has to die sometime, so that’s not the death he’s talking about. The death here is what the Bishop just read: the lake of fire. That’s not us wishing death on anybody; the Bible says it.

precepts.why: Read by the other speaker. “But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul”: against the Lord; you wrong your own soul. “All they that hate me love death”: the Bible says if you hate the Lord, you love death. The group that ran up out of here fits that verse.

Also read by the other speaker. “Seek not death in the error of your life: and pull not upon yourselves destruction with the works of your hands”: you’re getting yourself the death; you’re causing it. “For God made not death”.

“But ungodly men with their works and words called it to them”: with their actions and their words, their murmurings, they called death to themselves. “For when they thought to have it their friend”: they thought it was righteousness, even though it was death. “Because they are worthy to take part with it”: worthy of dying, based upon their words and their works. A speaker adds: anyone receiving that should say thank you, this is an opportunity for me to save my life, because you’re warning me of what the Most High said. Instead they say I hate you, so they don’t believe the scriptures and don’t want correction.

sense.text: “One of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues”: that’s what we read a few weeks ago in Revelation 16 about the destruction that comes upon America and the UK. “Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb’s wife”: jump back to verse 2; the bride, the Lamb’s wife, is New Jerusalem that’s coming down from heaven.

“He carried me away in the spirit to a great and high mountain”: the kingdom is going to be the highest city on the planet. “And shewed me that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God”: people ask why it still says descending out of heaven; I’ll show you later in the chapter.

precepts.why: Read again as the precept for the bride. “For I am married unto you”.

Because of “Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb’s wife”. “For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ”: we’re being prepared just like a bride prepares herself for that marriage day, to meet our husband, the Lord. We are the virgins, like it said in Matthew about the ten virgins, five wise and five foolish; I pray those of us that have remained fall into the five wise virgins.

The great and high mountain. “The mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains”: you’re going to have to look up to the kingdom of the Lord. It’s going to be the highest city on the planet; you’re going to see it for miles and miles. “And all nations shall flow unto it”: people get confused here and say all nations come into Jerusalem.

“All the nations shall be gathered unto it”: that’s what we just read. Verse 18 explains the all nations: “In those days the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel”. The house of Judah and Israel will be coming from all nations, “out of the land of the north to the land that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers”. This explains the bottom of Isaiah 2:2.

sense.text: “Having the glory of God”: now he’s going to describe the kingdom.

“Twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels”: there’s twelve black angels standing at those twelve gates. “Names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”: on the gates to the kingdom the only names written are the names of the twelve tribes of Israel. There’s no gate called Negro Baptist, no gate called Latino Catholic. Those denominational names your parents go by were all concocted by their enemies, the so-called white man: Jehovah’s Witness, Seventh-day Adventist, Protestant, Mormon, Islam, Rastafarianism, all that garbage. None of those names are on the gates.

“The wall of the city had twelve foundations”: the foundation is the ground. “The names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb”: their names will be etched in the twelve foundations around the kingdom of God on earth.

“The length is as large as the breadth”: the length and the width are equal, like a perfect square. “An hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel”: this is beyond our understanding. A regular cubit for us is two or three feet, but we can’t go by today’s measurements. The measuring of the cubit is going to be astronomical for the size of an angel.

precepts.why: To show that a cubit today is different than back in the day. “Wherefore are unto they whom thou hast now brought forth like those that were before, but less of stature?”. “Consider thou therefore also, how that ye are less of stature than those that were before you”: size was different in the past. “And so are they that come after you less than ye”: as time goes on, we get smaller and smaller. Esdras and them were bigger than we are now.

sense.text: “The city was pure gold, like unto clear glass”, and the foundations “garnished with all manner of precious stones”. We are so used to living around concrete. The Most High knows these elements affect us differently, like drinking out of a paper cup or a gold cup; being around gold and these elements will deal with us on another level, with the spiritual world. I see through a glass darkly; that’s all I can say. When you read in Exodus about the ephod, it’s the same elements that are going to be with the kingdom of heaven on earth.
“And I saw no temple therein”: you think you’re going to see another building inside those gates, but there’s no temple in there; it’s only the Lord and the Father in there.

“The city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon”. “For the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof”: it means exactly what it says. There’s still going to be a sun, a moon and stars, but within the gates of the kingdom they’re not going to need that light, because God himself and Christ will be the light therein.

precepts.why: “God is light, and in him is no darkness at all”: so when Revelation says the glory of God did lighten it and the Lamb is the light thereof, it means exactly that.

The thought may be that we’re not going to have a sun or a moon. Yes we are. “The light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun”: in the kingdom the moon is going to be as bright as the sun. “And the light of the sun shall be sevenfold”: the sun is going to be seven times brighter. But in the temple they’re not going to need it.

sense.text: “The nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it”: Isaiah 60 explains it. Like we always say, the New Testament is an abbreviated version of the Old Testament; the Old goes into a lot more detail.
“The gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there”: we just read that in Isaiah 60:20. Write that down.

“They shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it”: we’re going to bring all their wealth, because everything belongs to us. The world was made for us; we got to get out of that low self-esteem. To the nations holding all these diamonds, we’re going to say thank you for holding it for me. Remember when we left Egypt, we took all the Egyptians’ wealth, because it was ours anyway.

precepts.why: “The forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee”: the forces of the Gentiles means the wealth of the Gentiles. Camels, dromedaries, gold and incense come. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: this is why I waited, because when it talked about the kingdom descending from heaven, it’s just saying that’s how beautiful it’s going to look. “For in my wrath I smote thee”: slavery, colonialism. “But in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: Christ dying on the cross for us. “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually”: so Isaiah 60:11 goes with Revelation 21:24-25 combined. “The nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”: when we send our men out to gather the kings of the nations and a nation don’t want to come and bring their wealth, they shall be utterly wasted, and we’re going to drag their kings to the kingdom. Everybody is going to bow down and submit that Christ is the Lord. “To beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious”: the place of his feet is the kingdom. “All they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet”: they’re going to bend on their knees, and their face is going to be at our feet; that’s how low they’re going to be.

“That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow”: y’all be reading the New Testament and not getting no understanding. How are they going to bow? Isaiah 60:14 tells you: bending, at the soles of our feet. Will you submit that Jesus Christ is Lord, yea or nay? When they say nay, out come the chains. Y’all got this fairy tale that when Jesus returns every tongue just confesses; that’s why you need the Old Testament to explain things in detail.

“Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated”: everyone hated us. “Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles”. “I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness”: we’re going to have offices in the kingdom, and tax collectors to collect the tax from the Arabs and the Chinese; that’s the wealth coming up to us. “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: within our borders, but outside our borders, when we got to take them down, there’s going to be a lot of violence. “But the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light”: didn’t we just read that in Revelation 21? “Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself”: that’s talking about our understanding. “The days of thy mourning shall be ended”: he’s going to wipe away all tears. “Thy people also shall be all righteous”: sisters say they got a problem with seven women taking hold of one man, but this means men and women; ain’t going to be no niggerdom, no deadbeat daddy syndrome, ever again. We’re going to be filthy rich, the top nation. “A little one shall become a thousand”: that’s how many kids we’re going to have. “I the Lord will hasten it in his time”: that’s why seven women shall take hold of one man; women are going to outnumber men once again.

To prove there will be violence outside our borders. “And the nations were angry”: this is talking about the second coming of the Lord. So what do you mean they’re going to bow down willingly? They’re angry when he comes back. Oh, my pastor never told me that; your pastor’s a dummy.
The world was made for Israel. “All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes”.
“Because for their sakes I made the world”: the world was made for us. That’s what we all have to understand.

sense.text: “There shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination”: that’s what we read earlier in verse 8. “Or maketh a lie”: he’s serious about that thing; all them liars are not getting into the kingdom. “But they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life”: only those written in the Lamb’s book of life, so the only one getting into the kingdom is Israel.

precepts.why: Old Testament first, then New. “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince”: Michael the archangel, the captain of the host of the army of God. “A time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation”: that’s where them bombs hit, them nuclear explosions; this is the hour of temptation. “At that time thy people shall be delivered”: Daniel’s people, the Israelites. “Every one that shall be found written in the book”: the Lamb’s book of life.

“I will not blot out his name out of the book of life”: if we keep the works of the Lord, his laws, statutes and commandments, he’s not going to blot our name out. That’s heavy, because it’s letting you know that with your wickedness you can be erased. Judas Iscariot was blotted out; Dathan, Korah and On were blotted out.

Moses told you about the book of life; it’s not a new thing. “If not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written”: Israel gave Moses hell with all the murmuring, complaining, backbiting and whispering. The Lord was going to destroy all the Israelites and start over with Moses, and Moses said no, spare the rest. That don’t mean God forgave everybody; the Lord killed hundreds of thousands of Israelites. “Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book”: that’s a nice prayer, Moses, but whoever sins I’m blotting out. Korah’s crew, 250 princes of Israel, were put to death with their wives and kids, and 14,000 others that followed them. So y’all keep following these wicked people on YouTube and Facebook, shame on you. Another speaker has verse 32 read again and adds: don’t attach yourself to nobody. Those were princes, men of stature in the congregation; Satan always uses the princes, the captains, a deacon or a bishop. When your friend leaves the truth and you go with your friend, your name is blotted out too.

sense.text: Another speaker returns to verse 4, where the Bishop brought out that in the kingdom we’re not going to be sick or walking around with a cane. “Neither shall there be any more pain”: no more arthritis, no more pain, period, for the nation of Israel. We ain’t losing no eyesight, we ain’t going to need no glasses, no back pains, no going to the doctors no more. The nations are going to have their doctors set up for them.

precepts.why: Read by the other speaker. “Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died”: that’s a long time. “His eye was not dim”: at 120, your eyes usually start to get small; old age catches up on you, but that didn’t happen to Moses. “Nor his natural force abated”: it didn’t leave him. He wasn’t weak and feeble and shaking; you couldn’t test him. And that wasn’t even the kingdom yet; the Lord was dealing with Moses on a different level.
